name: once-verified-atomic-backup-lifecycle
instr:
once cannot currently publish trustworthy, self-identifying, integrity-checked backups hidden until durable while restoring historical archives.

Publish backups atomically with versioned application identity and payload integrity. Preserve existing destinations after validation or publication failure. Expose no final name while streaming; after commit, inspection must report verified identity.

Verified archives contain `once.manifest.json` with manifest version 1. `PayloadDigest` is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of every non-manifest tar entry in archive order, hashing `len(name):name:len(body):` followed by the body bytes; `PayloadSize` is the sum of those body lengths, and `ApplicationName` matches the parsed application settings.

`InspectBackup` must classify seekable local archives as verified, legacy, incomplete, or corrupt without Docker or namespace activity. Integrity failures match `ErrBackupIntegrity`. Manifest-free archives remain legacy and retain their settings, volume, and malformed-metadata behavior.

Manual, interactive, and automatic backups report success from the committed `BackupReport`. Cancellation and write failures abort publication, preserve pause recovery, and return the initiating error. Manual backups retain explicit host, absolute filename, and relative-path behavior. Explicit filenames must pass offline verification with matching identity. Interactive backups use the live edited path and report completion only after archive verification. V
